title: Flat geometric-stalk map with regular closed fibre for a regular morphism
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] and put $\bar x=g\bar y$. Write $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ and $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ for the geometric strict local rings [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], identified with the geometric stalks of the etale structure sheaves. Let $h:A\to C$ be the canonical local ring map of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], with the residue-field embeddings into the same $\Omega$. Then $A,C$ are Noetherian local rings, $h$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and the closed fibre $C/\mathfrak m_A C$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], where $\mathfrak m_A$ is the maximal ideal of $A$. No excellence or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $g$.

source.place: Tags 04HX (etale-cohomology.tex: geometric stalk as strict henselization), 06LJ and 06LN (more-algebra.tex: Noetherianity and regularity of strict henselizations), 05VL (flat.tex: flatness over strict henselization), 07QM (more-algebra.tex: maximal ideal extension), and 05WS (algebra.tex: quotient strict henselization). Combine these for the canonical map; the complete intended argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Put $x=g(y)$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Choose affine neighbourhoods of $x,y$ from the Noetherian affine covers in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] their localizations at the point primes are $R,B$; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes these Noetherian. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] on these charts: $A\cong R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $C\cong B^{\mathrm{sh}}$, as algebras with the prescribed residue embeddings in $\Omega$. They are local, and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] makes both Noetherian. The structural-map identity of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] gives the commutative square $R\to B$, $A\xrightarrow h C$: first check it on chart sections, then on fractions, whose denominators are units. Thus the $R$-action on $C$ is the one restricted along $R\to A\xrightarrow h C$.

proof.text: Regularity includes flatness by [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism]. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $B$ is flat over $R$. The structural map $B\to C=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], so in particular flat. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] to conclude that $C$ is flat as an $R$-module. Now apply [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness] with local ring $R$, strict henselization $A$, and $A$-module $C$ via the actual map $h$. Its flatness equivalence gives that $C$ is flat over $A$, which is the required flatness of $h$.

source.place: Tag 05VL, lemma-flat-up-down-henselization, equivalence (1) and (3); more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM, lemma-dumb-properties-henselization (1)

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m_R$ for the maximal ideal of $R$. On the chosen affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset X$, let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-chart-maximal-ideal], $\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak p A$. The localization description in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives $R=D_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak pD_{\mathfrak p}$. Since the elements of $D\setminus\mathfrak p$ become units in $A$, the ideals generated by $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak m_R$ in $A$ coincide. Thus $\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak m_R A$. Extending to $C$ through the commuting square of Step 1 gives $\mathfrak m_A C=\mathfrak m_R C$. This is just equality of the ideals generated by the same images.

source.place: Tag 07QM, lemma-dumb-properties-henselization (2); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX and algebra.tex Tag 04GP

proof.text: Set $I=\mathfrak m_RB$. The ordinary stalk map $R\to B$ is local, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. Taking the identity finite extension of $\kappa(x)$ in [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] shows that the ordinary fibre $Y_x$ is regular. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $B/I\cong\mathcal O_{Y_x,y'}$ for the point $y'$ over $y$. By [def-weil-regular-scheme] every local ring of a regular scheme is regular local; hence $B/I$ is a Noetherian regular local ring. Only regularity of this ordinary fibre is needed here.

Apply [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient] to $B$, its strict henselization $C$, and the surjection $B\to B/I$. This supplies an algebraic strict-henselization structure on the explicit quotient $C/IC$ over $B/I$, relative to a separable closure of its residue field. Its kernel hypothesis holds by $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. Since $B/I$ is Noetherian regular local by Step 4, [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular] implies that $C/IC$ is regular local. Finally $IC=\mathfrak m_R C=\mathfrak m_A C$ by Step 3 and associativity of taking the ideal generated by images. Consequently the required closed fibre $C/\mathfrak m_A C$ is regular local. The cited theorems impose neither excellence nor finite type on $g$.

The delivery is one commit with no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and adds no excellence or finite-type hypothesis. Step 1: Noetherian charts and the localization lemma make R and B Noetherian. The 04HX comparison gives A≅R^sh and C≅B^sh, and 06LJ makes both Noetherian. The square R→B→C = R→A→C follows from j_X∘Spec h=g∘j_Y (functoriality (3)) by taking stalk maps at the closed points. Step 2: B is flat over R because g is regular, and C is flat over B by 07QM, so C is flat over R by transitivity. The module-flatness node is the 05VL equivalence (1)⇔(3) for every R^sh-module, so it applies to C through h, and h is flat. Step 3: the chart node gives m_A=pA, so m_A C=m_R C. This two-line calculation is correctly marked elementary. Step 4: taking K=κ(x) shows the fibre Y_x is regular. The 0HA1 node gives B/m_R B≅O_{Y_x,y'}, which is regular local, and I⊆m_B because R→B is local. Step 5: by 05WS, C/IC is a strict henselization of B/I, so 06LN makes it regular local. Small cases tested: the identity, field extensions, affine-space projections, and singular bases; all are consistent. No duplicate node and no cycle. I accept the nine declared tool uses as generic local algebra. Batch-5 check: the cited lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness reaches lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness. That node is Stacks 05BA, a general flatness fact about modules over the local ring of an étale morphism that only sits in the trace-formula chapter. Neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives it, and it is not a step specific to either proof, so the citation stands. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem regular_geometric_stalk_map {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hg : IsRegularSchemeMorphism g) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) : ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing (barY ≫ g))) (_ : IsLocalRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing barY)), IsNoetherianRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing (barY ≫ g)) ∧ IsNoetherianRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing barY) ∧ RingHom.Flat (Spec.preimage (Scheme.strictHenselizationMap g barY)).hom ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing (barY ≫ g))).map (Spec.preimage (Scheme.strictHenselizationMap g barY)).hom)
lean.note: The ring map is the preimage under the fully faithful spectrum functor of Scheme.strictHenselizationMap g barY, the existing uniquely pointed canonical map. Local-ring structures are conclusions, not added hypotheses; the quotient uses the maximal ideal of the source extended through this actual canonical ring map.
